ui.title: Mars Station
ui.subtitle: Keep your crew alive until the ship home arrives.
ui.energyHelp: You have {cells} power cells today. There are never enough for everything.
ui.system.lifeSupport.help: Makes air and water for the crew.
ui.system.shielding.help: Protects the crew on solar storm days.
ui.system.greenhouse.help: Grows food for the next sols.
ui.system.comms.help: Needed to talk to Earth tonight.
ui.noComms: The antenna has no power tonight. No call with Earth.
ui.stubWarning: Placeholder data: this is NOT real NASA data yet.
avatar.morning.hello: Good morning, Captain! It is sol {sol}.
avatar.morning.flare: A class {flareClass} solar flare erupted on the Sun. This one really happened on {date}. Source: NASA DONKI.
avatar.morning.cme: A cloud of solar plasma left the Sun at {speed} km/s. It really happened on {date}. Source: NASA DONKI.
avatar.morning.cmeMars: NASA's model said this plasma cloud would reach Mars!
avatar.morning.forecastStorm: Earth warned us: a radiation storm may hit on sol {sol}.
avatar.morning.dust: Dust still covers the sky. Our solar panels make less power.
avatar.morning.lowAir: Captain, air and water are running low!
avatar.morning.lowFood: Captain, our food is running low!
avatar.evening.sep: A real radiation storm hit near Earth on {date}. Source: NASA DONKI. Each crew member got {dose} mSv today.
avatar.evening.normal: Each crew member got about {dose} mSv of radiation today. That's normal on Mars.
avatar.evening.medbay: {name} got too weak and went to the medbay.
avatar.evening.leak: Air is leaking through the damaged hull.
avatar.evening.starving: The crew is hungry and getting weaker.
avatar.evening.thinAir: The air is thin. The crew feels sick.
term.sol: A sol is a day on Mars. It is 39 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
term.dose: Dose is how much radiation a person has soaked up. We measure it in mSv (millisieverts).
term.sep: A radiation storm happens when the Sun throws out a burst of fast particles. Thick walls and shelters help.
term.shielding: Shielding is like a thick blanket against radiation. More power makes it stronger, but never perfect.
term.delay: Radio signals take 3 to 22 minutes to travel between Mars and Earth, so Earth's team answers once per sol.
event.radiation_storm.title: Radiation storm!
event.radiation_storm.desc: The radiation alarm is beeping! A burst of particles from the Sun is hitting the station.
event.radiation_storm.shelter.outcome: The crew is safe in the shelter, but nobody can work in the greenhouse today.
event.radiation_storm.keep_working: Keep working, collect storm data outside
event.radiation_storm.keep_working.outco: We got rare storm data, but everyone soaked up more radiation.
event.quiet_sol.title: A calm sol
event.quiet_sol.desc: Nothing is going wrong today. A good day for science!
event.quiet_sol.eva_samples: Send 2 explorers outside for rock samples
event.quiet_sol.eva_samples.outcome: Great samples! But outside, the explorers got more radiation, and they couldn't help in the greenhouse.
event.quiet_sol.lab_work.outcome: The lab used extra power, so we'll have a bit less tomorrow. One crew member skipped greenhouse work.
event.dust_storm.title: Dust storm!
event.dust_storm.desc: A huge dust storm is covering the Sun. Our solar panels will make less power. In 2018 a dust storm like this stopped the Opportunity rover forever.
event.dust_storm.brush_panels: Send someone out to brush the panels
event.dust_storm.brush_panels.outcome: Clean panels! Power is back sooner, but the cleaner got extra radiation.
event.dust_storm.wait_inside.outcome: Everyone stays safe inside, but we'll have low power for 3 sols.
event.hull_damage.title: The hull is cracked!
event.hull_damage.desc: Wind threw a rock against the station. There is a small crack and air is leaking out.
event.hull_damage.fix_now: Send 2 crew out to fix it now
event.hull_damage.fix_now.outcome: Fixed! But the 2 fixers got extra radiation and couldn't farm today.
event.hull_damage.fix_tomorrow.outcome: We'll lose some air tonight. Tomorrow 2 crew will go fix it.
event.hull_damage.ignore.outcome: Nothing spent today, but air will leak out every sol from now on.
event.system_failure.title: Greenhouse pump broke
event.system_failure.desc: The water pump in the greenhouse stopped working.
event.system_failure.repair_now.outcome: Repaired! It took two people all day and some extra power.
event.system_failure.live_with_it.outcom: The greenhouse will grow only half as much food for 4 sols.
pending.hull_repair: the crew must fix the hull today.
reply.forecast.storm: Earth says: we see a solar storm coming. A radiation storm may hit you on sol {sol}. Source: NASA DONKI.
reply.forecast.calm: Earth says: the Sun looks calm for the next 2 sols.
reply.science_report: Earth says: we got your science report! {points} science points counted. Great work!
reply.lost: Dust in the air blocked the radio. Our message did not reach Earth.
end.failed.crew: The whole crew ended up in the medbay at the same time.
end.stars.0: Mission failed. Let's look at what happened and try again!
end.stars.1: You survived, but the science mission is not done.
end.stars.3: Perfect mission! Nobody went to the medbay and everyone stayed under the safe dose.
end.realEvents: Real NASA space weather you met in this mission:
end.tip.lifeSupport: Tip: life support needs about 4 power cells every sol to keep up.
end.tip.crew: Tip: on storm days, use the shelter and the shield.
data.title: Where the data comes from
data.donki: Solar flares, plasma clouds and radiation storms come from NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database). They really happened on the dates shown. They were measured mostly near Earth, while Mars was somewhere else in its orbit, so we say 'this really happened', not 'this hit Mars'.
data.rad: The everyday radiation on Mars comes from the RAD instrument on the Curiosity rover: about 0.64 mSv per day on the surface.
data.simplified: What we simplified: one sol in the game is one real day of space weather. Storm damage to health is made stronger so you can feel it in a 15-sol game.
